Mrs. Twiss has a wide, ruddy visage. When flushed, her face can turn a dark violet color.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XIV. MRS. HECTOR TWISS MAKES A CALL P25](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0025)_

## History

Born into the [Methodist](../codex/factions.md#methodist) faith, Hector Twiss was forced by his wife to convert to Presbyterianism and strictly adhere to [Presbyterian](../codex/factions.md#presbyterian) ways for the rest of his life. Following his death, he was remembered in the community, while his widow, Mrs. Hector Twiss, continued to involve herself in church affairs and local family matters.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P5](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0005), [v5 CHAPTER XIV. MRS. HECTOR TWISS MAKES A CALL P0](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0000), [v5 CHAPTER XIV. ## Quotes

> “Why, Mr. Ashdown,” she uttered, amazed. “You are surely cr—this cannot be your intention. It is necessary that you reconsider—reflect upon every benefit I am able to offer her.”

> "I assume this is yet another piece of your children’s mischief. No respectable woman belongs in a location like this. Hand over my umbrella and allow my departure. Never again will I step foot inside your church or your manse."
>
